skill.name: growth-strategy
skill.description: Design growth strategies, GTM plans, growth loops, and ethical experiments with clear metrics and guardrails.
skill.summary: Plan ethical growth initiatives with loops, activation metrics, experimentation discipline, and privacy-aware measurement.
skill.author: ClementWalter

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives after contextual review. The flagged external-command patterns are Markdown code fences in an output template, and the reconnaissance flags are ordinary growth-strategy prose.

static_findings.snippet: | Paid      | Revenue → reinvest in ads → more revenue        |

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 173 starts a Markdown text fence for an output template. It is documentation, not Ruby or shell backtick execution, and it contains no command to run.
Line 188 closes the same Markdown code fence. This is formatting for a proposed initiative template, not executable code or command substitution.
The phrase "Avoid vanity metrics" is business analytics guidance. It does not request host, network, identity, or environment reconnaissance.
The paid growth loop example describes reinvesting revenue in advertising. It is a marketing model, not a request to inspect system information.
The "Avoid" section introduces cautions against AI content spam and brand risk. It contains no operational instruction for reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Growth teams often chase tactics without clear loops, metrics, or guardrails. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code shape focused growth plans and experiments.
actual_capabilities: Defines North Star Metrics and weekly input metrics for growth planning.
Frames growth loops for viral, SEO, paid, sales, and product-led motions.
Builds experiment plans with hypotheses, segments, metrics, guardrails, and kill criteria.
Recommends high-impact tests for onboarding, pricing, referrals, landing pages, and lifecycle messaging.
Applies privacy, deliverability, and ethical red lines to growth tactics.
Provides RICE and ICE scoring guidance for experiment prioritization.
limitations: It does not calculate statistical sample sizes automatically.
It cannot validate analytics data quality without user-provided instrumentation details.
It does not replace legal review for privacy, advertising, or platform compliance.
Its recommendations need domain context, traffic levels, and business constraints.

use_cases.title: Create a SaaS GTM Plan
use_cases.description: Map a product-led growth motion into loops, activation milestones, and measurable weekly inputs.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Experiment Backlogs
use_cases.description: Score growth ideas with RICE or ICE and convert top ideas into test-ready briefs.

use_cases.title: Review Growth Tactics for Risk
use_cases.description: Check lifecycle, referral, and AI-assisted campaigns against privacy, deliverability, and trust guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Find Growth Loops
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a product or service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this growth-strategy skill to identify the strongest growth loops for my product. Ask for any missing context first, then suggest input metrics and guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an Experiment Brief
prompt_templates.scenario: Turning one idea into a structured test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn this growth idea into an experiment brief: [idea]. Include hypothesis, target segment, success metric, guardrails, implementation steps, measurement, and kill criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Backlog
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to score these growth ideas with RICE or ICE: [ideas]. Explain the assumptions, rank the experiments, and identify the first three tests to run.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Privacy-Aware Growth System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced strategy across acquisition, activation, retention, and measurement.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this growth-strategy skill to design a privacy-aware growth system for [business]. Include loops, instrumentation, experiment cadence, lifecycle constraints, ethical red lines, and reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan an onboarding experiment for a B2B SaaS product with low activation.
output_examples.output: A structured initiative brief with the onboarding lever, activation hypothesis, primary input metric, churn and support guardrails, implementation steps, measurement plan, and stop conditions.

output_examples.input: Prioritize five growth ideas for a new marketplace.
output: A ranked experiment list using RICE or ICE.
Assumptions behind reach, impact, confidence, and effort.
Recommended first test with success metrics and guardrails.

output_examples.input: Review an AI content campaign before launch.
output_examples.output: A risk-focused review covering quality control, SEO risk, user trust, platform policy constraints, and safer experiment alternatives.

best_practices: Start with the growth loop and input metric before choosing tactics.
Define guardrails and kill criteria before launching each experiment.
Use first-party data and incrementality tests when attribution is noisy.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize vanity metrics that do not affect growth loops.
Do not ship spam, fake reviews, dark patterns, or deceptive consent flows.
Do not scale AI-generated content without quality review and clear user value.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create growth strategies, GTM plans, experiment briefs, growth loops, and tactic reviews.

faq.question: Can it plan A/B tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It structures hypotheses, target segments, metrics, guardrails, sample rules, and kill criteria.

faq.question: Does it support product-led growth?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers activation, onboarding, retention, monetization, and product-driven acquisition loops.

faq.question: Does it replace analytics tooling?
faq.answer: No. It guides measurement design, but it needs data from your analytics and experimentation systems.

faq.question: Can it review risky growth ideas?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks tactics for spam, dark patterns, deceptive pricing, privacy concerns, and platform limits.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Founders, growth teams, product managers, and marketing operations teams can use it for disciplined growth planning.
